issue.body:
When using Oracle in a docker container, the first time the container is run it takes a _long_ time to startup as lots of files are unpacked, etc.

The suggestion here is to create an Oracle-XE container using the base image from Oracle and then run `docker commit` to create an updated image based on the unpacked XE installation. The following startup times are then much faster (seconds as opposed to many minutes)

(This may be related to the long startup time reported in #1292)

issue.body: Oracle container currently uses default JDBC wait strategy, which tries to query the database. However, for this is known to falsely work on the Oracle container (https://github.com/testcontainers/testcontainers-java/issues/1292).  Instead, we should wait for a healthy docker health check.

issue.title: Custom MSSQL Server Container fails to complete initialization when running with Testcontainers

repository.name: testcontainers-java
repository.description: Testcontainers is a Java library that supports JUnit tests, providing lightweight, throwaway instances of common databases, Selenium web browsers, or anything else that can run in a Docker container.

issue.body:
Hello!

I'm working on adding new tests to run it with Testcontainers for MSSQL Server. I tried to do it in similar way that was used to support tests for MySQL but failed.

I work on Windows10 64 Pro and use the following tools:
- Docker Desktop v. 3.1.0 (Linux containers) Engine 20.10.2
- Java 8
- JUnit 5
- Testcontainers 1.15.1
- mssql-jdbc-8.4.1.jre8.jar

I built custom docker image based on MSSQL Server. If I run it manually via docker command in terminal window 

`docker run -d --name mssql-base -p 11433:1433 test-mssql-base:latest`

it will be successfully initialized - new database and test user will be created. 

But when MSSQL Server container is lauched by Testcontainer it fails to execute SQL scripts  to complete initialization:

`/opt/mssql-tools/bin/sqlcmd -S localhost -U sa -P "<password>" -d master -i create_test_database_and_user.sql`

`/opt/mssql-tools/bin/sqlcmd -S localhost -U sa -P "<password>" -d master -i create_tables.sql`

According to docker container log it fails with following error:

`Sqlcmd: Error: Microsoft ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server : Login failed for user 'SA'..`

I attached archive with example of Dockerfile and scripts to build custom MSSQL  Server docker image [build-docker-image.zip](https://github.com/testcontainers/testcontainers-java/files/5850185/build-docker-image.zip) as well as archive [unit-tests.zip](https://github.com/testcontainers/testcontainers-java/files/5850205/unit-tests.zip) with Unit test to reproduce the issue.
 
 P.S: I had to use [this workaround](https://github.com/testcontainers/testcontainers-java/issues/1292#issuecomment-548301153) to make Wait strategy to work for MSSQL Server container.
